standard_prerequisites.name: Soundness of schemas
standard_prerequisites.statement: If a relation R has one of the listed properties (serial, reflexive, symmetric, transitive, euclidean), every instance of the corresponding axiom schema (D, T, B, 4, 5) is true in every model with that relation (thm:soundschemas, sibling frame-definability unit).
standard_prerequisites.use: Opens the proof: all instances of D and 5 are true in serial euclidean models, so by soundness a countermodel need only be serial euclidean and invalidate one instance of 4.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 1601-1603): KD5 is not equal to KT4, and KT4 equals S4.

Reduction (proof lines 1606-1609): by the soundness-of-schemas theorem all D and 5 instances hold in serial euclidean models; by soundness it suffices to exhibit a serial euclidean model with a world falsifying an instance of 4.

Countermodel evaluation (proof lines 1609-1611): in the serial euclidean model of fig:KD5not4 (delivered as context span, lines 1614-1637) the formula Box p implies Box Box p fails at w1, which separates KD5 from KT4 = S4.
proof_roadmap: Reduce by soundness to exhibiting a serial euclidean countermodel.
Read the four-world serial euclidean model from the delivered figure.
Evaluate the 4 instance at w1 to conclude the separation.
difficulty_reason: Logic separation by countermodel (statement 1601-1603, proof 1605-1612): soundness reduction plus explicit evaluation of the failing 4 instance at a named world of the delivered figure; the figure is load-bearing and enters as a context span. H2.
